both BAV and valve replacement correct the acquired von WILLEbrand disease associated with aortic stENosis (AS).

aortic valve replacement corrects the haematological abnormality of the acquired von Willibrand syndrome of aortic stenoses and the decrease of the VWF cleaving protease ADAMTS- 13 activity may play a part in this correction.

aortic valve replacement and balloon aortic valvaloplasty reverse the acquired von WILLEBRAND syndrome of aortic stenoses and that the postoperative fall in VWF cleaving protease (Adamts-13) is a major determinant of the postoperative increase in VWF: Rco to VWF: ag ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ADAMTS- 13 in aortic stenoses.

the role of von Willebrant factor (VWF), a large multimeric protein, and the protease ADAMTS- 13 in the development of aortic stenoses and the effects of balloon valvulotomy (valve dilatation) and aortic valve replacement.
the acquired von WILLEBRAND DISEASE (vWD) in aortic valve stenosis (Aortic stenosis).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acquired von Wilebrand syndrome of AS is reversed by AVR and that the haematologic benefits of AVR may be in part due to a post-operative decrease in ADAMTS13 activity.
the haematologic abnormalities of AS, the acquired von Wilebrand disease, are corrected by both BAV and by AVR, and that the fall in ADAMS-13 activity following AVR contributes to this correction.
aortic valve replacement corrects the haematologic abnormalities of the acquired vWD of aortic stenoses by both reducing shear stress and decreasing postoperative levels of ADAMTS- 13.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ADAMTS- 13 is a key regulator of VWF in the acquired von Wilebrand disease of AS, that ADAMTS 13 activity falls following AVR but not BAV and that this change may contribute to the haematologic improvement following AVR.
aortic valve replacement corrects acquired von Wille brand disease in patients with a stenotic aortic valve by reducing shear stress and by decreasing ADAMTS- 13 levels.
aortic valve replacement corrects acquired von Willebrant disease by increasing the activity of VWF and decreasing the ADAMTS- 13 activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acquired von Wilebrand Syndrome is a reversible condition.
aortic valve replacement corrects the acquired von Wilebrand syndrome in patients with aorti stenosis.
ADAMTS- 13 activity decreases after valve replacement and this is a factor contributing to the improvement in the von Willebrand profile.
